question: Where is the Mahabodhi Temple, included in the UNESCO World Heritage Site list located?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bodh Gaya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Mahabodhi Temple is located in **Bodh Gaya**, Bihar, India.
 
• This temple is a UNESCO World Heritage Site since **2002**.
 
• The Mahabodhi Temple complex is revered as the place where **Gautama Buddha attained enlightenment**.
 
• The temple stands adjacent to the sacred Bodhi Tree under which Buddha is said to have attained enlightenment.
 
• Bodh Gaya is one of the most important and sacred pilgrimage sites for **Buddhists** from around the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Site:**

 
 
• It is a landmark or area with legal protection by an international convention administered by the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization.
 
• These sites are designated as having cultural, historical, scientific, or other forms of significance.
 
• The program aims to catalog and preserve sites of outstanding importance to the common heritage of humanity.
 
 
 
• **Bodhi Tree:**
 
 
• The tree under which Siddhartha Gautama, who later became Buddha, meditated and attained enlightenment.
 
• The Bodhi Tree is a large and ancient Sacred Fig tree (Ficus religiosa).
 
• The current tree in Bodh Gaya is considered to be a direct descendant of the original tree.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Bodh Gaya:**
 
 
• Bodh Gaya is one of the four major pilgrimage sites related to the life of Gautama Buddha, the others being Kushinagar, Lumbini, and Sarnath.
 
• The site attracts pilgrims from all over the world, including many from Tibet, Bhutan, and Japan.
 
 
 
• **Architecture of Mahabodhi Temple:**
 
 
• The temple's main structure is 55 meters tall and features a central tower surrounded by four smaller towers, all constructed in the same style.
 
• The temple is built using bricks and is one of the oldest brick structures still standing in India.
 
• The architecture of the Mahabodhi Temple is a fine example of the Gupta period with its distinct features and carvings.
